text: The text contrasts the presentation of the theme of good versus evil in J.R.R. Tolkien's 'The Lord of the Rings' and C.S. Lewis's 'The Chronicles of Narnia'. Both works share the prevalent theme of good versus evil, but they differ in their complexity and moral clarity. 'The Lord of the Rings' presents a complex world with a clear distinction between the forces of good and those of darkness. In contrast, 'The Chronicles of Narnia' often blurs this line by introducing characters who waver between sides, thus presenting a more nuanced view of morality.
